newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SOCIALISTS HANG ON TO POWER AS PRLT STORMED.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SOCIALISTS HANG ON TO POWER AS PRLT STORMED.

text.p: Bulgaria's ruling Socialist Party (BSP) postponed voting on a crucial "salvation declaration" in which the oppostion calls for early general poll, as protesters stormed parliament's building for the first time in history.
Dozens of riot police clashed with as many demonstrators inside the building and tried to disperse them with hoses and tear gas.
Thousands of teargassed protesters outside parliament overturned and demolished BMW and Mercedes cars of deputies parked near the building.

"For those who can hear us inside parliament, please stop. Bulgaria is headed for a state of emergency. Parliament is our only institution which can resolve our economic and political voes," private radio station Darik appealed to protesters tearing down the building.
All windows of paliament's ground floor of the Renneissance bulding, one of Sofia's architectural landmarks, were smashed.
"I hope there is enough of common sense not to impose a state of emergency," said Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) deputy and ex-prime minister Filip Dimitrov.

Parliament speaker Blagovest Sendov was meeting with heads of parliamentary groups to discuss the crisis as some Interiour Ministry troops arrived as enforcement to cordon off deputies trying to leave the building. None had left so far.
Police sprayed jets of water on protester from parliament's windows.
"We will remain in parliament to press for early general election as this is the only way out of the crisis," head of UDF parliamentary group Yordan Sokolov told Darik radio.
"What is happening in and outside parliament is the justified wrath of people brought to desperation," he added.
Some 50,000 massed around parliament, blowing whistles, burning red flags and effigy representing the BSP.
People were bringing hot drinks and food for the supporters. Nearby art-galleries served coffee and tea free of charge.

On Wednesday the Socialists had nominated the powerful Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev as prime minister in place of outgoing Zhan Videnov, who resigned on December 21 after severe criticism of his management of the economy.
Dobrev, perceived as the Socialist's strongman, was prevented from leaving parliament by a volley of snwowballs earlier on Friday.
Demonstrators hurled chunks of ice and heavy snowballs at socialist deputies which tried to leave parliament.
The opposition says the BSP has failed to tackle the country's economic crisis and now lacks support to form a government.
Voters delivered a powerfull no-confidence vote two months ago by electing the opposition's presidential candidate Petar Stoyanov with a 60 percent majority.
President-elect Stoyanov was carried away by his bodyguards after he teargassed when he tried to appease the protesters through a loudspeaker.
Ambulances took away protestors and riot policemen who collapsed after tear gas attacks. The emergency hospital reported 15 injured so far. Teragassed protesters were still arriving at the hospital.
"The BSP which led the country to its gravest crisis in history has no right to rule," said Sokolov.
One quarter of the country's banks are placed in receivership and tripple-digit inflation has eroded incomes to below the existential minimum.
The lev collapsed at 660 to the dollar on Friday, from 70 a year ago. It lost 35 percent of its value against the dollar since the beginnig of the year.

As soon as parliament appoints a new cabinet the International Monetary Fund plans to negotiate implementaton of a tough fixed exchange regime as last resort to restore confidence in the crumbling economy.
